argument_summary: The admissible record does not support clean compliance under the stated policy predicate, because the affected housing voucher recertification segment remains exposed, the initial 7% gate does not exclude that segment, and the only risk-acceptance record is an incomplete, unapproved draft that does not address the exposure. The narrower, supportable position is that certification can be defended only as a monitored, reversible launch with explicit disclosure of the unresolved limitation and residual risk, using the aggregate readiness pass margin, absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents, rollback capability, and deployment monitoring as operational mitigation rather than as a cure for the disclosure weakness.
claims_about_business_cost: No business-cost claim is offered as a basis to override the policy predicate. The argument for proceeding is limited to admissible operational mitigation evidence, not schedule pressure or launch velocity.
claims_about_policy: Under the policy text, rollout controls and post-launch monitoring mitigate a material model-card weakness only if they exclude the affected use case or are paired with reviewed risk acceptance explaining why exposure is acceptable. The admissible evidence shows neither condition is met here. The policy-consistent defense is therefore not that the weakness is cured, but that any certification must be caveated, must preserve the countervailing record, and must explicitly disclose the unresolved limitation affecting the named launch use case.
concessions: The housing voucher recertification segment remains below target on income-change documentation guidance.
The initial rollout gate does not exclude the affected housing voucher recertification segment.
The current risk-acceptance document is a draft, has no completed approval line, and does not address the exposed segment.
Rollback capability, monitoring, and a 7% initial rollout do not by themselves remove disclosure duties under the stated policy.
